result.summary: The page is mostly well-formed, but the promotional banner has a serious contrast problem: the headline and subtext are rendered in white/very light text on a pale green background, making them nearly illegible. Other elements (header, chips, carousels, bottom nav) appear intact; the partially visible carousel item at the right edge and the card cut off at the bottom are expected scroll behavior and not defects.

issues.description: In the '3 free deliveries for you' promo banner, the heading and the 'Use code TALLINN3 at checkout · min. order €10' subtext are white/very light text on a pale mint-green background, resulting in very low contrast and poor readability.
issues.suggestion: Use a dark green or near-black text color on the light green banner (or darken the banner background) so the headline and promo code text meet WCAG AA contrast ratios (at least 4.5:1).

issues.description: The promo banner's low-contrast text also makes the promo code (TALLINN3) hard to notice, weakening the visual hierarchy of the call-to-action area compared to the high-contrast 'Order now' button.
issues.suggestion: After fixing contrast, consider emphasizing the promo code (e.g., bold or a chip/badge style) so it stands out as actionable information.
